rituals.name: THE SECURE PENDING BOX
rituals.unique_game_move: Imagine Container → Name Stored → Close Container
rituals.recognition_cue: Unfinished material needs a boundary, not denial.
rituals.immediate_need: Unfinished material needs a boundary, not denial.
rituals.match_reason: Trauma time collapse · Unfinished material needs a boundary, not denial.
rituals.goal: Unfinished material needs a boundary, not denial.
rituals.steps:
1. Imagine Container — Imagine a container whose lock, size, material, and location feel credible.
2. Place Cannot — Place only what cannot be processed now inside it.
3. Name Stored — Name what is stored and when it will be revisited, ideally with support.
4. Close Container — Close the container and reorient to the next task for today.
rituals.win: ✓ Someone else’s share moved back out of my hands.
rituals.winReward: ✓ Someone else’s share moved back out of my hands.
rituals.tips:
• Let distance survive the pull toward flooding through.
• You can honour a painful memory and still refuse flooding through.
• Choose gentle orientation before deciding that the past feeling close will last.
• Let steadiness set the direction when the old danger signal feels loud.
• A memory can feel current while still belonging to another time.
rituals.supports:
• Let distance survive the pull toward flooding through.
• You can honour a painful memory and still refuse flooding through.
• Choose gentle orientation before deciding that the past feeling close will last.
• Let steadiness set the direction when the old danger signal feels loud.
• A memory can feel current while still belonging to another time.
rituals.mindBend: The small room separates the pull of trauma time collapse from the command your mind thinks it heard.
rituals.formulaFlow: Imagine Container → Place Cannot → Name Stored → Close Container
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Do not use containment to postpone urgent safeguarding or necessary care.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.
rituals.feedbackOptions: My body is still activated | The fear is still loud | The urge is still strong | My thoughts are still racing | I feel less steady
rituals.ifBetter: Some orientation returned around small room. Keep another safe person or professional involved; do not handle trauma time collapse alone.
rituals.ifALittle: A little steadiness is not enough for trauma time collapse. Stay with verifiable facts around small room and involve another safe human now.
rituals.ifNotYet: Do not keep cycling exercises for trauma time collapse. Use small room only to stay oriented while you seek appropriate human or emergency support.
rituals.nextMechanismRule: If THE SECURE PENDING BOX misses what you need for trauma time collapse, use a behavioural-experiment ritual next and avoid repeating a game whose purpose was to work with the idea that unfinished material needs a boundary, not denial.

rituals.name: BUILD SAFE-ENOUGH, NOT PERFECT
rituals.unique_game_move: Place Five → Rehearse Specific → Strengthen Safe-Enough
rituals.recognition_cue: A believable refuge works better than fantasy pressure.
rituals.immediate_need: A believable refuge works better than fantasy pressure.
rituals.match_reason: Trauma time collapse · A believable refuge works better than fantasy pressure.
rituals.goal: A believable refuge works better than fantasy pressure.
rituals.steps:
1. Place Five — Picture a place using five sensory facts and one control feature: an exit, boundary, companion, or adjustable distance.
2. Rehearse Specific — Practise entering through a specific cue and leaving on purpose.
3. Strengthen Safe-Enough — Strengthen the detail that produces the clearest bodily yes.
rituals.win: ✓ Progress no longer has to audition as perfection.
rituals.winReward: ✓ Progress no longer has to audition as perfection.
rituals.tips:
• Use a safe current anchor to stay connected with present safety.
• Use today’s difference to keep the old danger signal from becoming everything.
• Use gentle orientation before turning a memory surge into a life rule.
• Let a safe current anchor reduce the pressure that a memory surge creates.
• Keep rushed closure from turning a painful memory into a bigger problem.

rituals.name: ONE-WORD LIGHT TOUCH
rituals.unique_game_move: Apply Quiet → Use Word → Name Lightly
rituals.recognition_cue: Name enough to see; not enough to build a story.
rituals.immediate_need: Name enough to see; not enough to build a story.
rituals.match_reason: Scarcity thinking · Name enough to see; not enough to build a story.
rituals.goal: Name enough to see; not enough to build a story.
rituals.steps:
1. Apply Quiet — As events arise, apply a quiet category: hearing, planning, heat, remembering, pressure.
2. Use Word — Use one word once, then return to the raw event.
3. Name Lightly — If a label starts producing analysis, name that ‘explaining’ and release it.
rituals.win: ✓ One word was enough; explanation did not get a sequel.
rituals.winReward: ✓ One word was enough; explanation did not get a sequel.
rituals.tips:
• Choose accuracy over proving something to one-sided evidence.
• Use contrary evidence to make the mental filter more manageable.
• One dose of the missing facts can reopen better judgement.
• Do not use confirmation seeking as proof that a narrowed conclusion is correct.
• Do not use cherry-picking as proof that the mental filter is correct.
rituals.supports:
• Choose accuracy over proving something to one-sided evidence.
• Use contrary evidence to make the mental filter more manageable.
• One dose of the missing facts can reopen better judgement.
• Do not use confirmation seeking as proof that a narrowed conclusion is correct.
• Do not use cherry-picking as proof that the mental filter is correct.
rituals.mindBend: Use the bright bridge on scarcity thinking: what feels like a wall may only be the first handle you missed.
rituals.formulaFlow: Apply Quiet → Use Word → Name Lightly
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Drop noting if labels become compulsive, critical, or distancing.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.
rituals.feedbackOptions: The thought still feels true | I still need certainty | The loop restarted | I cannot see another angle | I am still stuck on the same question
rituals.ifBetter: ONE-WORD LIGHT TOUCH worked here; your response to scarcity thinking just gained another option.
rituals.ifALittle: Good—scarcity thinking moved but did not clear. Tell ThinkStill what is still strongest around bright bridge; the next move must target a different mechanism.
rituals.ifNotYet: No forcing it. ONE-WORD LIGHT TOUCH is a miss for scarcity thinking this round. ThinkStill should leave bright bridge behind and switch to a different mechanism.
rituals.nextMechanismRule: If you finish ONE-WORD LIGHT TOUCH and still need help with scarcity thinking, follow it with a sensory-grounding ritual so the next method differs from the name enough to see, not enough to build a story approach.

rituals.name: CLOSE THE MICRO-GAPS
rituals.unique_game_move: Choose Precise → Track Interval → Let Practice
rituals.recognition_cue: Meditative flow is repaired one break at a time.
rituals.immediate_need: Meditative flow is repaired one break at a time.
rituals.match_reason: Attention fragmentation · Meditative flow is repaired one break at a time.
rituals.goal: Meditative flow is repaired one break at a time.
rituals.steps:
1. Choose Precise — Choose an anchor and notice the precise moment contact breaks.
2. Return Instead — Instead of judging the distraction, shorten the delay before returning.
3. Track Interval — Track the interval between noticing and reconnection.
4. Let Practice — Let practice end after one stretch with visibly fewer or shorter gaps.
rituals.win: ✓ The practice has fewer leaks than it did a minute ago.
rituals.winReward: ✓ The practice has fewer leaks than it did a minute ago.
rituals.tips:
• Give less input more authority than multitasking.
• One moment of one manageable task can protect more focus.
• Take less input seriously when mental noise feels overwhelming.
• Let a quieter mind have more influence than multitasking today.
• Use one manageable task to keep too many demands from becoming everything.

rituals.feedbackOptions: I still cannot start | I keep getting distracted | There are too many steps | I lost the thread | I cannot switch or stop
rituals.ifBetter: That shift counts. The low spark gave you a route through attention fragmentation that actually moved something.
rituals.ifALittle: Good—attention fragmentation moved but did not clear. Tell ThinkStill what is still strongest around low spark; the next move must target a different mechanism.
rituals.ifNotYet: No forcing it. CLOSE THE MICRO-GAPS is a miss for attention fragmentation this round. ThinkStill should leave low spark behind and switch to a different mechanism.
rituals.nextMechanismRule: If attention fragmentation is still dominant after CLOSE THE MICRO-GAPS, choose a problem-solving ritual as the next doorway instead of rerunning the work with the idea that meditative flow is repaired one break at a time method.

rituals.ritual_name: CHANGE THE RHYTHM, CHANGE THE STATE

rituals.immediate_need: Emotion maintains itself through tempo as well as story.

rituals.goal: Emotion maintains itself through tempo as well as story.

1. Cadence — Notice the cadence of speech, movement, or breathing.
2. Choose Opposite — Choose an opposite rhythm: agitated becomes deliberate, collapsed becomes lightly brisk, looping becomes irregular.
3. Observe Emotional — Maintain the new tempo through one simple task and observe the emotional shift.

rituals.winReward: ✓ I changed the tempo and gave the state a different rhythm to follow.

• Keep physical discomfort separate from your worth.
• A calmer rhythm can teach the body that intensity is not danger.

rituals.unique_game_move: Name Appears → Replace Identity
rituals.recognition_cue: Identity claims must show recent action evidence.
rituals.immediate_need: Identity claims must show recent action evidence.

rituals.name: BORROW STILLNESS FROM THE WALL
rituals.unique_game_move: Rest Gaze → Don't Match → Let Facts
rituals.recognition_cue: Let an unmoving object prove that movement is not the whole field.
rituals.immediate_need: Let an unmoving object prove that movement is not the whole field.
rituals.match_reason: Sensory disconnection · Let an unmoving object prove that movement is not the whole field.
rituals.goal: Let an unmoving object prove that movement is not the whole field.
rituals.steps:
1. Imagine Still Line — Picture a stable horizontal line or horizon.
2. Compare — Notice its imagined stillness beside the movement inside your body and mind.
3. Allow Both — Do not force inner movement to match the line.
4. Borrow Stability — Let the stable image become a reference for one slow breath.
rituals.win: ✓ Stillness entered the scene, so movement stopped being the whole field.
rituals.winReward: ✓ Stillness entered the scene, so movement stopped being the whole field.
rituals.tips:
• Keep mental drift separate from your worth.
• A single sensory detail can reconnect attention with the present.
• Do not use story chasing as proof that a floating mind is correct.
• Allow mental drift; then move toward steadiness.
• You can respect mental drift without obeying story chasing.

rituals.name: SORT THE SOUNDS BY DISTANCE
rituals.unique_game_move: Identify Nearest → Move Attention → Let Far
rituals.recognition_cue: Urgency shrinks when hearing regains depth.
rituals.immediate_need: Urgency shrinks when hearing regains depth.

rituals.steps:
1. Identify Nearest — Spot the nearest sound, one mid-distance sound, and the farthest audible layer.
2. Move Attention — Move attention outward through those distances, then back once.
3. Let Far — Let the far sound widen the perceived space around the closest one.

• Choose a short pause even if decision pressure has not disappeared.

PLAY TIME

45–60 seconds

GOAL

Difficulty can signal growth, danger, novelty, or bad design.

1. Use Evidence — Classify the strain using evidence.
2. Stop Novelty — If danger, stop; if novelty, allow learning; if skill growth, dose it; if poor design, simplify the system.
3. Respond Category — Respond to the category instead of interpreting all effort as failure.

WIN

✓ I identified what kind of effort this was before deciding what it meant.

TIPS

• Choose one deliberate pause even if autopilot has not disappeared.
• Use one deliberate pause to stay connected with choice.
• Use a different response when autopilot starts narrowing your options.
• When automatic behaviour rises, return to a brief interruption.
• Choose a brief interruption because more control deserves protection.

MIND BEND

The low lane separates the pull of automatic-pattern blindness from the command your mind thinks it heard.

FORMULA FLOW

Use Evidence → Stop Novelty → Respond Category

SAFETY

PAUSE
Persistent pain, exhaustion, or mental change needs professional assessment.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.unique_game_move: Hold Cue → Identify Future → Receive Support
rituals.recognition_cue: Uncertainty is not evidence for your favourite meaning.
rituals.immediate_need: Uncertainty is not evidence for your favourite meaning.

rituals.recognition_cue: Perceiver and perceived need not stay rigidly opposed.
rituals.immediate_need: Perceiver and perceived need not stay rigidly opposed.

3. Place Reality — Refuse to place all reality on either side.

• Thoughts can stay present while you choose not to merge with them.

rituals.challenge: Holding too many steps in mind in the moment
rituals.primary_trigger: Holding too many steps in mind in the moment
rituals.unique_game_move: Working-memory overload via empty runway: One clean signal → One quiet funnel → Interrupt the compass → Short relay first → One real button
rituals.recognition_cue: Let One Quiet Funnel hold the return cue outside your head so working memory can breathe.

rituals.goal: Let One Quiet Funnel hold the return cue outside your head so working memory can breathe.
rituals.steps:
1. One clean signal — Use empty runway between the start in front of you and what usually follows; let empty runway insert one harmless action before the reflex.
2. One quiet funnel — Keep one view of the start in front of you inside empty runway; keep one return cue inside empty runway and close the menu after this one selection.
3. Interrupt the compass — Find the next automatic link in the start in front of you; put empty runway in that gap so empty runway makes the old chain miss one turn.
4. Short relay first — Move empty runway outside the start in front of you; let empty runway find three ordinary details and keep one steady in view.
5. One real button — Move empty runway outside the start in front of you; let empty runway find three ordinary details and keep one steady in view; Use One real button if attention slips.

• Insert a clean gap; use outside details.
• Change the sequence; widen the spotlight.
• Interrupt before action; borrow the room.
• Stop the chain once; give attention somewhere else.

rituals.challenge: You are waiting for perfect closure
rituals.primary_trigger: You are waiting for perfect closure
rituals.unique_game_move: Closure perfectionism via side light: Return to plain anchor → Clean tree first → Side roots first → Narrow road first → Hidden chapter first
rituals.recognition_cue: Take side light off the whole problem and aim it at one result: release without approving.
rituals.situation: You are waiting for perfect closure
rituals.immediate_need: Take side light off the whole problem and aim it at one result: release without approving.
rituals.match_reason: Closure perfectionism · Take side light off the whole problem and aim it at one result: release without approving.
rituals.goal: Take side light off the whole problem and aim it at one result: release without approving.
rituals.steps:
1. Return to plain anchor — Use side light as home base during the bigger question; feel side light through contact and find three neutral sights or sounds.
2. Clean tree first — Place only the bigger question inside the active window of side light; keep one controllable next move inside side light and make no second selection until this one lands.
3. Side roots first — Touch side light while the bigger question is loud; keep side light with one stable contact, then name three ordinary things nearby.
4. Narrow road first — Place the rigid rule behind the bigger question at side light; bend it through side light by one safe degree.
5. Hidden chapter first — Use side light to expose the 'must' inside the bigger question; let side light run one harmless counterexample.

GOAL

2. Low clock first — Reduce the fear in front of you to one open lane in warm anchor; keep one stable external detail inside warm anchor and give the unpicked options no turn in this pass.

4. Clean wall first — Anchor at warm anchor inside the fear in front of you; let warm anchor keep you located while your eyes find three safe details.
5. Find warm anchor — Touch warm anchor while the fear in front of you is loud; keep warm anchor with one stable contact, then name three ordinary things nearby.

• Compare before concluding; orient outward.
• Leave one rival explanation; borrow the present.

Warm anchor does not force calm; Add the pulse simply stops urgency owning the next move.

rituals.ritualText:
THE THREAD GETS ONE VOTE

PLAY TIME

45–60 seconds

GOAL

Use Gentle Lens First to stop retrying an unwinnable case and return one choice to the present.

1. Low margin first — Anchor at small thread inside the thought in front of you; let small thread keep you located while your eyes find three safe details.
2. Gentle lens first — Put small thread around one stopping point in the thought in front of you; Small thread keeps one move active and the rest offstage for now.
3. Hidden timeline first — Use small thread as home base during the thought in front of you; feel small thread through contact and find three neutral sights or sounds.
4. Use narrow window — Let small thread hold one clean entrance into the thought in front of you; remove blame from small thread and leave one clear request.
5. Say one door — Put the opening sentence for the thought in front of you on small thread; let small thread hold fact first, effect second, request last.

WIN

✓ Gentle lens first landed—you stopped the stale loop.

TIPS

• Feel stable contact; build the first sentence.
• Name the room; remove blame words.
• Use one plain fact; rehearse once.
• Orient outward; open with facts.
• Borrow the present; say less, clearer.

MIND BEND

Gentle lens first lets uncertainty remain while small thread refuses to promote it to danger.

FORMULA FLOW

Low margin first → Gentle lens first → Hidden timeline first → Use narrow window → Say one door

SAFETY

PAUSE
Stop if the exercise increases disorientation, trauma flooding, compulsive checking, or severe distress. Seek appropriate professional support when symptoms are persistent, intense, or unsafe.

rituals.steps:
1. Touch one coin — Put steady key at the doorway of the thought in front of you; begin with the easiest real action that reaches steady key.
2. Hold soft spotlight — Use steady key to light the thought as a mental event inside the thought in front of you; anything beyond steady key does not enter before the current move ends.
3. Find narrow bookmark — Let steady key lower the entry into the thought in front of you; change the task at steady key from untouched to begun.
4. Near forecast first — Place the thought in front of you inside steady key as a happening in time; let steady key cut the future verdict attached to it.
5. Extract one page — Use steady key to name the thought in front of you plainly; keep steady key with what happened and leave identity conclusions outside.
